_README: THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH. `py trade.py` with no arguments reads
it and runs. It is written once, when absent, and never overwritten by a
The `run` block is read ONCE at startup: the batch, the shop model and
the loop's arithmetic are built around it, so it is not safe to change
mid-run. Everything else is re-read at the top of EVERY cycle, so a
change lands on the next cycle and never mid-action.
A malformed or invalid file is IGNORED with a warning: the run keeps the
values it already has rather than stopping.
Changes are applied ALL OR NOTHING, because these knobs constrain each

_NOTES.CHAOS_ENABLED: run the chaos pass at all
_NOTES.CHAOS_ROWS: bundles to keep on the board
_NOTES.CHAOS_RESTOCK_AT_OR_BELOW_ROWS: rebuy at or below this many
_NOTES.CHAOS_MARGIN_FLOOR: min Set-over-Core spread per unit (chaos only)
_NOTES.CHAOS_UNDERCUT: Alz shaved off a chaos listing
_NOTES.RESTOCK_TARGET: core min: hard floor per restock
_NOTES.BUY_MAXIMUM: core max: soft ceiling, and what a restock runs to
_NOTES.RESTOCK_AT_OR_BELOW_ROWS: TRIGGER: start restocking a Core once it is down to this many rows or fewer. The chaos equivalent is CHAOS_RESTOCK_AT_OR_BELOW_ROWS.
_NOTES.CORE_ROWS: TARGET: rows each ordinary Core keeps on the board, the CHAOS_ROWS idea per type. Trigger and target are different questions: at or below the trigger it starts buying, and it stops at the target. The target also bounds how many rows a restock may reserve, which is what stops a type being refused over rows it would never have used.
_NOTES.CORE_ROWS_BY_ITEM: per-item overrides of that target, every Core listed so the value in force is readable without knowing the default. The Core targets plus CHAOS_ROWS must fit the 30-row shop or the file is refused.
_NOTES.PRICE_DIFF_FLOOR: profit margin a normal Core's Set must clear to be worth buying
_NOTES.PRICE_DIFF_FLOOR_BY_ITEM: per-item overrides of that margin. Every normal Core is listed below so the value in force is readable without knowing the default. MIND THE GRADE: 'Force Core(High)' is a substring of 'Force Core(Highest)' and they are different items with different margins -- matching is on an exact name, never a prefix. An item named here that is not a favourite is REFUSED, so a typo cannot silently restore the default.
_NOTES.run: startup only: the shape of the run itself
_NOTES.COST_FLOOR_ON_RELIST: never relist below what the stock cost
_NOTES.CHAOS_RECIPE: which craft recipe chaos uses. 1 = [1500] Chaos Core Set (x1) under the 1000-1999 tier; 2 = [2500] Chaos Core Set (x3) under 2000-2999, which takes 3 Cores and yields 3 Sets per craft, so a third of the craft operations for the same stock. Two fixed clicks, no OCR: the tier, then the recipe under it. Both points assume the tree is in its resting state (all tiers collapsed), which is what the craft window opens to.
